answer: Unrepeatable Challenge Lattice. Each new identity must solve a fresh challenge derived from a hidden karst of precomputed partial solutions, seeded by its own public key. The atlas of valid solution paths is never published; only verifiers hold it. Identities must submit answer hashes that collide with their key at a declared nadir of difficulty, and each solved challenge retires one path permanently. An attacker cloning an identity reuses a retired path and fails. Cost: one unique precomputation per identity, roughly hours of compute, non-transferable and non-refundable.
